note.question: What changes when lane’s algorithm is revisited?
note.overview: In 1964, Kenneth Lane proposed an algorithm to optimize the production schedule of a single-metal, single-processor open pit mine. For this, he proposed a policy based on varying, over time, the so-called “cutoff grade”—or grade threshold used to determine if extracted material should be ore (processed material) or waste (thrown away). Lane’s algorithm had a profound impact on the mining industry.
